newsitem.title: USA: U.S. unveils Bangladeshi-type microbank program for poor areas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. unveils Bangladeshi-type microbank program for poor areas.

text.p: Housing Secretary Henry Cisneros unveiled a $20 million pilot program Thursday to help revitalize poor neighborhoods by establishing Bangladeshi-type tiny, community-owned banks.
Joined by First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, Cisneros said the program would bring needed credit to areas shunned by larger, commercial banks.

"Small loans can bring remarkable results -- more people working and fewer on welfare, homeowners moving into areas instead of moving out, homes being repaired instead of falling into decay," Cisneros said at a press conference here.
Clinton said the program, called the Community Empowerment Banking Initiative, was inspired by the success of similiar banks she had visited in Bangladesh, Bolivia and Chile.
"This is part of returning to communities assets that have been stripped from them because of the changes in the global economy in the last decade," the first lady said.
Under the pilot program, the federal government will provide seed money to establish banks which will then sell shares to residents and local business owners for $10 to $30 each.
The banks will also receive financial backing from local governments and corporations and then make loans for neighborhood projects, mortgages and home improvements.
The first three banks will be established in Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Maryland, and a rural section of Mississippi.

In Washington, the new bank will combine a $3.5 million grant and $5 million loan guarantee from the federal government with about $85 million in other public and private funds to make $60 million of loans over the next five years.
In Mississippi, the bank will receive $3.5 million plus a $5 million loan guaranty to combine with $12.4 million of other public and private resources.
And the program will give the Baltimore bank $1.5 million plus an equal amount in a loan guaranty.
